Amazon Bedrock quotas and usage

Current account limits and observed usage. Explore models, review capacity, and identify data that needs attention.

Usage over time

One identifier at a time, preserving the original metric dimensions.

Historical usage is compared with today's quotas. Token estimates do not reproduce the max_tokens reservations used for capacity control. A low estimate does not rule out throttling.

Series with observed data

Volumes by identifier, without adding overlapping aggregates of the same traffic.

Current quotas

Applied values and AWS defaults are kept separate.

A quota defines a limit, not guaranteed available capacity. A percentage appears only when the quota, metric, and units have a confirmed mapping.

Catalog and availability

Availability reported by the API, without running inference.

A catalog entry does not prove your application can invoke the model. IAM, SCPs, endpoint policies, and provider prerequisites can still restrict access.

Inference profiles

Source Region, type, and reported destinations. Profiles do not represent independent quotas.

Provisioned Throughput

Existing resources and allocated units, separate from allocation quotas.
